'''Luz Josefina Martinez-Miranda''' (8 September 1956 – 27 April 2026<ref>[https://physicstoday.aip.org/obituaries/luz-josefina-martinez-miranda Luz Josefina Martínez-Miranda]</ref>) was an American-Puerto Rican physicist. She was an associate professor in the College of Materials Science and Engineering at the [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]]. Martinez-Miranda was an [[List of American Physical Society Fellows|APS Fellow]] and was the first female president of the [[National Society of Hispanic Physicists]].<ref name=":3" />

== Early life and education ==
Martinez-Miranda was born in [[Bethesda, Maryland]], and moved to Puerto Rico at the age of five. Her parents were both originally from Puerto Rico and were both chemists.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Martinez-Miranda |first=Luz |year=2002 |editor-last=SACNAS |title=SACNAS Biography Project |url=https://www.aip.org/sites/default/files/history/teaching-guides/sacnas/SACNAS_Biographies.pdf }}</ref> She attended high school in Puerto Rico at [[University High School (San Juan)|University High School]],<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Luz Martinez-Miranda - Physicist Profile Detail Page |url=https://www.compadre.org/careers/physicists/Detail.cfm?id=884 |access-date=2023-09-12 |website=www.compadre.org}}</ref> and went on to receive her bachelor's and master's degrees in physics from the [[University of Puerto Rico]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luz Martinez-Miranda - professor |url=https://www.compadre.org/careers/physicists/Detail.cfm?id=884 }}</ref> While studying at the university's [[University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus|Río Piedras campus]], she concurrently attended the Conservatory of Music of Puerto Rico, and earned a degree in musical performance with a specialization in piano performance.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Madren |first=Carrie |date=23 September 2011 |title=Luz Martinez-Miranda riding new wave in liquid crystal research |url=https://www.aaas.org/luz-martinez-miranda-riding-new-wave-liquid-crystal-research |access-date=11 September 2023 |website=AAAS}}</ref>

She graduated with her PhD in 1985 from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT). While at MIT, she was one of only 8 women of the 68 people in the physics program.<ref name=":1" /> Her doctoral advisor was [[Robert Birgeneau]] and her thesis was titled "Crossover Behavior and Fluctuations in the Vicinity of a Liquid Crystal Multicritical Point."<ref name=":2" />

== Career ==
After receiving her PhD, Martinez-Miranda held positions at [[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]] and the [[United States Naval Research Laboratory|Naval Research Laboratory]].<ref name=":2" />

In 1995, she joined the faculty of the [[University of Maryland, College Park]], and helped in the design of its junior materials laboratory.<ref name=":2" /> She was an undergraduate advisor for the Materials Science and Engineering Department at the University of Maryland. She studied the interaction of liquid crystal with nanoscale materials for engineering and biological applications.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Luz Martinez Miranda |url=https://mse.umd.edu/clark/faculty/688/Luz-Martinez-Miranda }}</ref>

She was the third president and the first female president of the [[National Society of Hispanic Physicists]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Luz Martinez-Miranda is a 2020 ADVANCE Honoree |url=https://mse.umd.edu/news/story/luz-martinezmiranda-is-a-2020-advance-honoree |access-date=2023-09-11 |website=mse.umd.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Martinez-Miranda's research focused on the interaction of liquid crystal with nanoscale materials.<ref name=":3" />

== Personal life ==
In addition to piano, Martinez-Miranda played the [[harpsichord]], specializing in Baroque music.<ref name=":4" /> Dr. Martinez Miranda passed away in 2026.

== Awards and honors ==
Martinez-Miranda was awarded the status of [[Fellow]] in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellow Archive |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=2017-04-20 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> after she was nominated by the [[Forum on Education Abroad|Forum on Education]] in 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |title=APS Fellows 2007 |url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2007&unit_id=&institution= |access-date=2017-04-20 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref> for ''sustained achievements in recruiting, mentoring, and advancing women and [[Minority group|minorities]] in [[physics]]; for engaging [[K-16 education|K-16]] students in the excitement of research; and for being a role model through her research to understand [[liquid crystal]] systems and further their application.''
* Fellow, American Physical Society (APS), 2007
* Visiting Faculty Appointment to the Centre de Recherche Paul Pascal, 2006
* Fellow, American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS), 2004
* Boricua College Professional Achievement Award in Science, 2004
* NSF Career Advancement Award, 1997
* W.M. Keck Foundation, Engineering Excellence Teaching Award, 1995
* Fellow, American Ceramic Society, 1994
* NSF Visiting Professorship for Women, 1994–1996.<ref name=":0" />
